text.p: A fugitive former New Jersey prosecutor, on the run from authorities for more than a week, shot himself dead Tuesday after being tracked down by federal marshals, officials said.

Former Somerset County prosecutor Nicholas Bissell had been the subject of a nationwide manhunt since he disappeared on Nov. 18, two days before he was to be sentenced on an array of federal criminal charges.
Authorities said marshals had traced Bissell to Laughlin, Nevada, and were talking to him when he put a gun to his head and pulled the trigger. He was declared dead at a nearby hospital.
Bissell had snipped his electronic monitoring bracelet and left a suicide note before vanishing from his home in Franklin Township, New Jersey, but authorities doubted its validity.

He was scheduled to be sentenced last Wednesday in U.S. District Court in Newark, New Jersey, on 30 charges, including fraud and tax evasion. Faced with a minimum sentence of six-and-a-half to 10 years in prison, he had been free under home confinement on $300,000 bail.

Bissell was convicted of skimming $146,000 from receipts of a gasoline filling station he partly owned to support a lavish lifestyle of fancy cars and jewelry. He was also convicted of professional corruption, misconduct and abuse of power, including ordering the destruction of a suspect's written request for an attorney and lying to investigators.
